undecided.quote: "Begich has 118,337 first-choice votes, or 48.8% of the vote." / "Hill has 99,240 votes, or 40.9% of the vote."
undecided.note: No call found. Ranked-choice tabulation scheduled for 18 Nov 2026 per the Anchorage Daily News article (paraphrased by the fetch tool, not quoted); certification 25 Nov. FairVote (updated 14 Nov) quote: "In these preliminary results, Nick Begich leads with 48.0% of first choices, to Bill Hill's 41.6%." and its unofficial simulated ranked-choice count has Begich winning 52-48. Wikipedia infobox: Elected = TBD, Begich (R) 47.71%, Hill (nonpartisan) 41.72%, 97% reporting as of 14 Nov. Begich (Republican) is favoured but nothing is called.

undecided.quote: Tessa Lynn Hodge, Dem: 105,541 votes, 49.2 percent / Jay Obernolte, Rep: 109,037 votes, 50.8 percent; "November 14, 2026, 5:16 p.m."
undecided.note: California Secretary of State count (as relayed by the fetch tool) shows Obernolte (R) ahead by 3,496 votes; no call found. NBC News pages (updated 4 Nov) show no "Projected Winner" for CA-23. Wikipedia California article footnote: not called by the Associated Press as of 10 Nov. Wikipedia main article per-state table counts California as 48 D / 4 R, i.e. it counts Obernolte's lead.

undecided.quote: Runoff "Dec. 12": Democrat Patricia "Pat" Moore (18 percent) and Republican Gabe Firment (17 percent) advance (fetch-tool rendering of the article; nine-candidate field).
undecided.note: Confirmed runoff. Runoff date 12 Dec 2026, Pat Moore (D) vs Gabe Firment (R). Wikipedia Louisiana article agrees (Moore 17.9, Firment 17.2) and states: "In races where no candidate receives over 50% of the vote, runoff elections will take place on December 12, 2026." Article describes a jungle (all-candidate) ballot on 3 Nov because party primaries were postponed.

undecided.quote: "only Democrat Chauna Banks (50,878 votes) and Republican Blake Miguez (50,213) advance to the runoff."
undecided.note: Confirmed runoff, Chauna Banks (D) vs Blake Miguez (R). WAFB does not give the date for the 6th; date 12 Dec 2026 comes from the Wikipedia Louisiana article's general statement. Republican Rick Edmonds was third, 972 votes behind Miguez (possible recount/challenge risk not checked).

undecided.quote: "The Associated Press has not called the race for Minnesota's 1st Congressional District." / "DFL challenger Jake Johnson has 322 more votes than Republican incumbent Brad Finstad."
undecided.note: Recount expected after the State Canvassing Board meets 19 Nov (KTTC: "A request for a recount cannot be made until after the state's certification"; Fox 9: State Canvassing Board meets Nov. 19). Wikipedia marks Jake Johnson (DFL) as elected (see disagreements); I found no source newer than 9 Nov stating a call. Johnson (D) leads.

undecided.quote: "the results are not yet certified." (Foxx trails Hubbard by 331 votes after the Friday canvass; Foxx has not conceded)
undecided.note: Chuck Hubbard (D) leads Rep. Virginia Foxx (R) by ~331 (WRAL 13-14 Nov; WUNC 10 Nov: "With all provisional ballots counted, Hubbard holds a lead of 325 votes."). Recount request deadline noon Tue 17 Nov; State Board certifies multi-county races 24 Nov (WUNC). Wikipedia: Elected = TBD, Hubbard 48.7 vs Foxx 48.6.

undecided.quote: "It wasn't immediately clear if their Democratic opponents would call for recounts." (Rouzer leads Kimberly Hardy by 2,311 votes)
undecided.note: David Rouzer (R) leads. WRAL does not number the districts; district 7 = Rouzer comes from Wikipedia (Rouzer 49.8 vs Hardy 49.1, Elected = TBD). Recount-eligible.

undecided.quote: "It wasn't immediately clear if their Democratic opponents would call for recounts." (Harrigan leads Ashley Bell by 2,509 votes)
undecided.note: Pat Harrigan (R) leads. District number from Wikipedia (Harrigan 49.6 / 146,590 vs Bell 48.7 / 144,081; elected field blank). Recount-eligible.

undecided.quote: "Victoria Broderick won with 48.9% of the vote, 0.1 points ahead of Scott DesJarlais." / "Results are complete but unofficial until county election commissions certify them by November 23, 2026."
undecided.note: Victoria Broderick (D) leads Rep. Scott DesJarlais (R) by ~280 votes (95,585 to 95,305). WSMV 4 Nov: "Democrat Victoria Broderick will win the race to represent Tennessee's Fourth Congressional District" based on Secretary of State unofficial totals; NewsChannel 5: "DesJarlais has not called to concede." Search-result snippets (pages 403, not opened) say the AP had not called it and ~700 provisional ballots were to be counted, Davidson County on 16 Nov. No AP call found. Wikipedia: Broderick shown leading, TBD, but the main article counts Tennessee as 1 D / 8 R. Status is best described as "uncalled by AP, Democrat projected by Secretary of State unofficial count".

disagreements.note: Wikipedia infobox after_election = Jake Johnson, 163,061 (50.0%) vs Finstad 162,740 (49.9%), result box marks DFL gain, no text about a call. KTTC (9 Nov) says the AP has not called it and a recount is anticipated after the 19 Nov state canvass. I found nothing newer than 9 Nov; Wikipedia may be marking the leader. Same leader in both; disagreement is only on called vs not.

Wikipedia footnote: AP had not called CA-4 as of 10 Nov. KQED AP results page: "Race called at 5:25 PM PT on November 13, 2026." Jones 52.5% (130,246) vs Thompson (D) 47.4%. Party is Democrat either way.

Wikipedia footnote: AP had not called CA-7 as of 10 Nov. The second page is the file's own source (NBC News Decision Desk, updated 4 Nov), which shows "Projected Winner" for Matsui 52.4% vs Mai Vang 47.6% at 94.1% expected vote. KQED CA-7 page returned 404; no AP call found. Both candidates are Democrats, so party is not in doubt.

Wikipedia infobox Elected = TBD (Elijah 49.7 vs Bale Dalton (D) 49.2). Spectrum News 13 (10 Nov, the file's own source) reports an AP call: "In District 7, Elijah defeated Democratic challenger Bale Dalton." 161,300 to 159,669. Wikipedia appears not updated.
Minor: Wikipedia infobox Elected = TBD although Westerman has 65.5%. Same winner and party; almost certainly an unfilled Wikipedia field.

party_totals.file: 257 Democrat, 169 Republican in 426 called races; 7 uncalled, 2 runoff (435 total)
party_totals.sources: Wikipedia national article (as of 11:00 AM EST 15 Nov 2026): results bar 257 D, 169 R, 9 TBD; infobox says 256 D (internal inconsistency on the page). Its per-state table (47 states, excluding AK, LA, MN which show no figures) sums to 254 D / 166 R; the file for the same 47 states has 252 D / 163 R called plus 5 uncalled (CA-23, NC-5, NC-7, NC-10, TN-4). The differences are exactly those 5 uncalled races counted by their current leaders (D: NC-5 Hubbard, TN-4 Broderick; R: CA-23 Obernolte, NC-7 Rouzer, NC-10 Harrigan). Every state total otherwise matches the file. Wikipedia also gives a national popular vote of about 56.2% D to 42.3% R, and Texas 14 D / 24 R is independently reported by Latin Times. A 257-169 split is consistent with the sources I could open; I did not find an official (AP or state) national tally to confirm it independently.

notes: Method: one full independent listing = English Wikipedia per-state 2026 House election articles, read by six helper agents via WebFetch (rendered pages truncated after ~300k characters, so the raw wikitext (action=raw) was used to fill gaps). Each Wikipedia winner/party was compared to the file by script (party exact, surname match); 346 districts agree on winner name and party. All name differences in agreeing rows are only formatting (middle initials, Nick/Nicholas, accents, Jr.). Caveats: (1) All Wikipedia readings went through the fetch tool's summarising model, so a single misread is possible. (2) Many Wikipedia articles are only partly updated; districts with blank winner fields were not counted as checked. (3) Wikipedia is not official; second sources were opened for each disagreement, but two of those second sources (CA-7 NBC, FL-7 Spectrum) are the file's own cited sources. (4) TN-4 and AK are not listed as disagreements: Wikipedia shows Broderick and Begich only as leading with Elected = TBD, consistent with the file. Ballotpedia main 2026 page returned an empty page. Web searches used: 13 of ~25; none refused. Background knowledge was not used to fill any result.
